transcript:
Header
Date: 2026-03-31
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE); Jordan Lee (Redwood SE); Carlos Mendes (Medexa - Head of ML); Aisha Rahman (Medexa - Infra); Tom Bennett (Medexa - Security); Leah Ortiz (Medexa - Product)

Summary: quick sync on Private VPC pilot - networking, routing, upgrade window, perf runs and follow-ups.

[00:00] Samira Khan: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda - networking updates, the control plane upgrade window, jordan will walk perf, and then open issues.
[00:28] Carlos Mendes: yeah thanks, uh we did a bit of prep on our side, aisha has been working on the firewall entries.
[00:45] Aisha Rahman: mmhmm, we opened the ticket last night, we added the outbound rules for 10.12.0.0/16 to the redwood control plane, but we had a question about the ip ranges for fallback regions. the spreadsheet had 3 ranges but they overlapped with our internal mgmt range.
[01:10] Jordan Lee: ok we can re-export minimal allowlist; samira i'll share the trimmed list after this call. there was also an issue where the pilot's NLB was doing source preservation and the control-plane was rejecting because of client ip mismatch; we recommended turning on proxy protocol or using the tcp passthrough.
[01:35] Tom Bennett: proxy protocol woudl be preferred? also any impact to our IDS? sometimes proxy protocol changes break our parsing.
[01:50] Jordan Lee: yeah good point, if you have an IDS that expects certain headers, proxy proto can confuse it. alternative is we can terminate TLS at the NLB and forward via private link to the agent, so the client ip stays in the x-forwarded-for header. there was a small mis-match earlier because of the NLB health check behavior, so we suggested marking the health check as tcp on the agent port.
[02:20] Leah Ortiz: sorry quick q, will that affect latency on the small responses? a lot of our calls are sub-100ms.
[02:32] Jordan Lee: should be minimal, the extra TLS termination is a few ms. the bigger wins are batching and kv cache - if you let the agent warm the KV cache with the common prefixes you see, we see 20-30% token latency improvements for our workload shapes.
[03:00] Samira Khan: quick check - carlos, are you still running the 2-stage routing test we asked?
[03:08] Carlos Mendes: yes, ran it yesterday, initial results are in the shared drive under "pilot/perf/results.csv". overall throughput is ok but there were a couple of 500s on long context. i think the kv cache miss pattern caused a fallback to the longer path.
[03:30] Jordan Lee: yep that matches, when the kv cache misses we fall back to the unpacked attention kernel which increases token time. for those long-context 5xxs we saw memory pressure on the pod - looks like we need the memory tuning flag in the agent (we mis-documented it in the initial runbook as mem_limit instead of mem_reserve).
[03:55] Aisha Rahman: oh that's why the pod restarted, we saw oomkill in the logs. can you share the exact agent flag name?
[04:05] Jordan Lee: it's --reserve-kv-memory, with boolean and MB flag, we'll put exact example in the runbook. sorry about the doc typo.
[04:22] Tom Bennett: on security, does the agent send any PII back to the control plane? we need to know what telemetry leaves our VPC.
[04:32] Jordan Lee: good call - standard telemetry is metrics and heartbeats, not payload. but because this is Private deployment, you can opt into no-control-plane telemetry; we also have an audit log option that stores request hashes only. we'll send the security whitepaper and the SOC2 excerpts.
[04:55] Samira Khan: tom we'll send the SOC2 pdf and the KMS integration doc after the call.
[05:04] Tom Bennett: great, that'd be helpful. also please note our KMS uses hardware-backed keys (HSM) and they require signing over an SR-req; do you support HSM workflows?
[05:18] Jordan Lee: yes we have integrations for AWS KMS and customer-managed keys via HSM in the private control plane, though the initial pilot used envelope encryption to avoid extra ops. we'll detail the HSM flow in the doc.
[05:40] Carlos Mendes: back to perf, jordan i saw the perf sheet mentions batching size 8 and auto-batching; can you explain the tradeoffs?
[05:50] Jordan Lee: sure - batching increases throughput by combining token work but it increases tail latency slightly. auto-batching tries to cap the batch by either time or token count; for your QPS profile i'd recommend target batch size 6-8 with a max delay of 20ms to keep tail below 200ms. also quantization on the model weights reduced memory by about 30% in our lab so you can run larger contexts without OOM.
[06:25] Leah Ortiz: did we test 8k context?
[06:29] Jordan Lee: we ran 4k earlier. for 8k we need a dedicated GPU type and a different kernel; jordan here: the plan for next week is the 8k run on p4d-8x or equivalent, which i'll schedule once we confirm capacity.
[06:50] Carlos Mendes: capacity wise, do we need dedicated? we don't want the shared hosted perf variance.
[06:56] Samira Khan: for consistent SLOs we recommend Redwood Dedicated but your pilot can still emulate with bigger instance sizes on private. dedicated gives SLA and reserved GPU pool.
[07:10] Tom Bennett: can you put the pricing delta in the same spreadsheet as the perf runs? makes it easier for security procurement.
[07:17] Samira Khan: yes will do.
[07:22] Aisha Rahman: networking question - we tried VPC peering but cross-account route tables didn't propagate, we had to hand-add routes per subnet. any way to simplify?
[07:35] Jordan Lee: if you do AWS Resource Access Manager and share the subnet, route propagation is easier; alternatively we support Transit Gateway for multi-account setups. we'll add both options in the network doc.
[07:50] Carlos Mendes: and what about egress IP stability? some of our compliance tests pin IP ranges.
[07:58] Jordan Lee: for stable egress IPs we support NAT gateway with Elastic IPs or use small set of static NAT egress via our private control plane - we'll provide a deterministic IP list for the pilot.
[08:20] Samira Khan: quick check on upgrade - we plan a control-plane agent upgrade next Friday, it'll bump the agent to 1.4.2 which includes the kv-reserve flag fix and better health check handling. any blockers?
[08:36] Aisha Rahman: we need a maintenance window - our team prefers evenings. can you provide the exact migration steps?
[08:44] Jordan Lee: yes the plan is rolling upgrade, agent restarts one node at a time, health checks ensure no traffic is drained incorrectly; we'll supply the script and a fallback rollback. it should be non-disruptive but we'll need you to confirm windows.
[09:00] Tom Bennett: do upgrades change audit log schema? procurement asked.
[09:06] Samira Khan: they shouldn't, major schema changes are versioned and communicated. minor fields can be appended but we keep backward compat for logs for one major release. we'll include schema notes.
[09:20] Carlos Mendes: ok next on issues - we saw an intermittent routing loop in the private agent logs. logs attached in shared drive as "agent-logs/loop-0319.log".
[09:31] Jordan Lee: looked - that's likely due to stale route cache after peering flaps; we added a TTL for route cache in 1.4 which should mitigate. the loop coincided with the peering flaps at 03:12 UTC.
[09:50] Aisha Rahman: is there a way to flush the route cache without full restart?
[09:55] Jordan Lee: yes there's an admin endpoint /admin/cache/flush which you can call locally in the VPC and won't affect control plane. we'll add curl examples to the runbook.
[10:10] Leah Ortiz: can someone summarize the blockers and owners?
[10:15] Samira Khan: sure - firewall allowlist (aisha), perf 8k run (jordan), SOC2 docs (samira/Tom), upgrade window (aisha + samira), route cache flush steps (jordan).
[10:35] Jordan Lee: for the perf run i'll also gather raw traces and KV-hit rates. if you can provide the representative prompt set carlos mentioned, we'll run against that to get realistic numbers.
[10:50] Carlos Mendes: will upload prompts to the shared drive by friday.
[11:05] Tom Bennett: on the compliance front, we also need the encryption-at-rest key lifecycle policy. do you have a template?
[11:12] Samira Khan: yes, we have a key lifecycle template, i'll attach it to the email with SOC2 docs.
[11:28] Aisha Rahman: tiny nit - the initial runbook referenced 'mem_limit' which confused our infra scripts; thanks for clarifying --reserve-kv-memory.
[11:40] Jordan Lee: yup sorry about that, fixed in the runbook already.
[12:02] Samira Khan: great, shall we confirm next sync - same time next week?
[12:10] Carlos Mendes: works for us.
[12:15] Leah Ortiz: fine with me.
[12:20] Samira Khan: ok we'll reconvene. thanks everyone.
